title: Lab 2 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Culturing Bacteria — isolation methods and combined media

questions.prompt: This plate shows colonies of more than one color and form. What kind of culture is it?
questions.explanation: Mixed culture: multiple species present. Most natural cultures and medical specimens are mixed.

why.A: A pure culture contains a single species — colonies would look alike.
why.D: Enriched describes the medium, not how many species are present.

questions.prompt: All the colonies on this plate look the same. What kind of culture is it most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Pure culture: a single species. Pure cultures rarely exist in nature but are needed for accurate diagnostic testing.

why.B: Mixed cultures contain multiple species with different-looking colonies.
why.D: A negative control should show no growth.

questions.prompt: Why is an isolated colony essential to generating a pure culture?

options.text: A colony originates from a single cell, so it contains a single species
A colony contains several species that grow at equal rates
Isolated colonies grow faster than crowded colonies do
Isolated colonies are always the disease-causing species

questions.explanation: A bacterial colony originates from a single cell that multiplies — so it contains a single species and can be subcultured as a pure culture.

why.B: A colony arises from one cell and contains one species.
why.C: The point is purity, not growth speed.
why.D: The colony is pure, but identification still must be done.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the quadrant streak plate method shown?

options.text: To count the number of live bacteria in a sample
To determine whether an organism ferments lactose
To obtain isolated colonies for a pure culture
To sterilize the agar surface before use

questions.explanation: The quadrant streak plate gradually 'dilutes' microbes across the agar so isolated colonies form in later quadrants.

why.A: Counting live cells is done with serial dilutions and plate counts.
why.D: Media are sterilized in the autoclave.

questions.prompt: While streaking quadrant 2, how many times do you drag the loop back through quadrant 1?

options.text: Never — each quadrant is streaked separately
Twice — then streak quadrant 2 without revisiting quadrant 1
Continuously while streaking all of quadrant 2

questions.explanation: Stab 3 times in clean agar, drag back through Q1 into Q2 twice, then streak Q2 without revisiting Q1. Repeat for Q3 and Q4.

why.A: You must drag back through Q1 to carry organisms into Q2.
why.C: The protocol drags back through Q1 twice; the loop isn't sterilized between quadrants.
why.D: After the two passes you streak Q2 without revisiting Q1.

questions.prompt: How long is the loop sterilized in the microincinerator, and how long does it cool?

options.text: Leave it resting in the incinerator between uses

questions.explanation: Sterilize the wire end for 10 seconds, then let it cool in the air for 15 seconds.

why.A: The protocol says 10 s in the incinerator, then 15 s to cool.
why.C: The protocol says 10 s in the incinerator, then 15 s to cool.
why.D: Never rest loops in the incinerator — they will break.

questions.prompt: When removing or replacing the cap of a culture tube, what do you do?

options.text: Pass the mouth of the tube in front of the incinerator three times
Set the cap down flat on the disinfected lab table
Invert the tube several times to mix the culture first
Dip the mouth of the tube into a beaker of alcohol

questions.explanation: Aseptic technique: remove the cap without setting it down and pass the tube mouth in front of the incinerator three times when opening and before closing.

why.C: Agitate by gently shaking — DO NOT INVERT.
why.D: The tube mouth is passed in front of the incinerator.

questions.prompt: Mannitol salt agar and MacConkey agar combine which two functional types?
questions.explanation: MSA and MacConkey combine selective and differential traits ('Wonder Twin powers, activate!').

why.B: MSA and MacConkey aren't described as defined.
why.D: They are not general purpose or reducing.

questions.explanation: Blood agar: enriched (blood supports fastidious growth) and differential (shows ability to lyse red blood cells — hemolysis).

why.A: That combination describes MSA and MacConkey.
why.C: Blood is a complex ingredient, so it isn't defined.
why.D: Blood agar adds blood (enriched) and shows hemolysis (differential).

questions.prompt: Citrate agar combines which three traits?
questions.explanation: Citrate agar: defined (known composition), selective (organisms lacking citrase don't grow), differential (detects citrate used as sole carbon source).

why.A: Citrate agar is defined (exact composition known), not complex.
why.B: It is selective and differential, not enriched or reducing.
why.D: It is defined, and selective/differential rather than general purpose.

questions.prompt: Neisseria spp. are capnophiles. What do they require to grow?
questions.explanation: Capnophiles need extra CO2 — e.g., Neisseria spp. grown in a CO2 incubation chamber.

why.A: Live hosts may be needed for obligate intracellular parasites.
why.C: Capnophile refers to CO2, not heat.

questions.prompt: Which statement about culturing obligate intracellular parasites is FALSE?

options.text: They grow well on nutrient agar plates
All viruses fall into this group
They may require eukaryotic cell cultures
They may require live animal hosts

questions.explanation: Obligate intracellular parasites (all viruses, Rickettsia, Chlamydia, Treponema pallidum) need living cells — cell cultures or live hosts — not artificial agar.

why.B: True — viruses are listed as obligate intracellular parasites.
why.C: True — they need living host cells.
why.D: True — some require live animal hosts.
why.E: True — along with Treponema pallidum and all viruses.

questions.prompt: Practice Problem A: prepare 300 mL of tryptic soy broth; the label says 42 g per 1 L. How many grams?

why.C: That divides 42 by 3 instead of multiplying by 0.3.

questions.prompt: Practice Problem C: prepare 3 L of urea broth; the label says 84 g per 1 L. How many grams?

why.A: That divides 84 by 3 instead of multiplying.
why.B: Grams and liters aren't added; multiply 84 × 3.

questions.prompt: Which procedure error would most likely give a streak plate with NO isolated colonies (heavy growth in every quadrant)?

options.text: Sterilizing the loop before starting the streak
Dragging the loop back through quadrant 1 while streaking every later quadrant

questions.explanation: Isolation depends on gradual dilution: only the first passes enter the previous quadrant. Re-entering Q1 repeatedly carries too many cells forward and prevents isolated colonies.

why.C: That's the correct step — it's what dilutes the organisms.
